# Environment Variables (https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/environment/)

## Minimum configuration [#minimum-configuration]

If the URL of your Uptime Kuma status page is `https://example.kuma-mieru.invalid/status/test1`, you need only one variable:

```ini title=".env"
UPTIME_KUMA_URLS=https://example.kuma-mieru.invalid/status/test1
```

For multiple status pages, separate the full URLs with `|`:

```ini title=".env"
UPTIME_KUMA_URLS=https://example.kuma-mieru.invalid/status/test1|https://example.kuma-mieru.invalid/status/test2
```

The template of the variables is `apps/web/.env.example`. Where you set the variables depends on the deployment method:

| Deployment method              | Where to set                                              |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Vercel, Netlify, EdgeOne Pages | The environment variable settings in the platform console |
| Docker Compose                 | `.env` in the repository root                             |
| docker run                     | `-e` options, or the file given with `--env-file`         |
| Run from source                | `apps/web/.env`                                           |

## When variables apply [#when-variables-apply]

| Variables                                                                          | Read                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS`, `UPTIME_KUMA_BASE_URL`, `PAGE_ID`, `KUMA_MIERU_*`, `FEATURE_*` | When the `generate` script runs. The result goes to `apps/web/config/generated-config.json` and `apps/web/config/generated/image-domains.json` |
| `STRICT_IMAGE_REMOTE_PATTERNS`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_ERROR_PAGE_DEV_MODE`                  | During `next build`                                                                                                                            |
| `ALLOW_EMBEDDING`                                                                  | While the server runs                                                                                                                          |

Hosting platforms run the `generate` script during the build. A Docker container runs it each time it starts. Thus:

- After you change a variable on Vercel, Netlify or EdgeOne Pages, redeploy.
- After you edit `.env` for Docker Compose, run `docker compose up -d --force-recreate`. The container then reads the environment variables again.

## Variable list [#variable-list]

| Variable                          | Required | Default                        | Description                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS`                | Yes\*    | None                           | Recommended. One or more full status page URLs. They can come from different Uptime Kuma instances |
| `UPTIME_KUMA_BASE_URL`            | Yes\*    | None                           | Legacy. Base URL of the Uptime Kuma instance. Used only when `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS` is not set         |
| `PAGE_ID`                         | Yes\*    | None                           | Legacy. Status page IDs, separated by commas. Used only when `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS` is not set         |
| `KUMA_MIERU_TITLE`                | No       | Title of the status page       | Title of the browser tab                                                                           |
| `KUMA_MIERU_DESCRIPTION`          | No       | Description of the status page | Description metadata of the page                                                                   |
| `KUMA_MIERU_ICON`                 | No       | Icon of the status page        | Page icon. It must come from the Uptime Kuma instance of the status page                           |
| `KUMA_MIERU_EDIT_THIS_PAGE`       | No       | `false`                        | Show the Edit This Page button                                                                     |
| `KUMA_MIERU_SHOW_STAR_BUTTON`     | No       | `true`                         | Show the Star on GitHub button                                                                     |
| `ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS`              | No       | `false`                        | Skip HTTPS certificate validation for runtime server requests to Uptime Kuma                       |
| `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`              | No       | `8000`                         | Timeout of runtime server requests, in milliseconds                                                |
| `REQUEST_RETRY_MAX`               | No       | `3`                            | Maximum number of retries for runtime server requests                                              |
| `REQUEST_RETRY_DELAY_MS`          | No       | `500`                          | Base interval between retries of runtime server requests, in milliseconds                          |
| `SSR_STRICT_MODE`                 | No       | `false`                        | Only the value is validated. It does not change the page behavior                                  |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_ERROR_PAGE_DEV_MODE` | No       | `false`                        | Show the full stack trace on the global error page. Written at build time                          |
| `ALLOW_EMBEDDING`                 | No       | `false`                        | Allow other sites to embed the dashboard in an iframe                                              |
| `STRICT_IMAGE_REMOTE_PATTERNS`    | No       | `false`                        | Allow only remote image domains on the allowlist                                                   |

\* Set either `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS` or `UPTIME_KUMA_BASE_URL` with `PAGE_ID`. If you set both, Kuma Mieru uses `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS`. If you set neither, the `generate` script stops with an error.

For the legacy names that start with `FEATURE_`, see [Legacy variable names](#legacy-variable-names). The Docker image has built-in defaults for some variables. With the `docker-compose.yml` of the repository, variables that are missing from `.env` go to the container as empty values. See [Docker](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/deploy/docker/).

## Status page addresses [#status-page-addresses]

### UPTIME_KUMA_URLS [#uptime_kuma_urls]

This is the recommended form. The value is one or more full status page URLs:

- Each URL has the format `https://<host>/status/<page ID>`. The part before `/status/` is the base URL of Uptime Kuma, and it can include a path prefix. The segment after `/status/` is the page ID.
- Separate multiple URLs with `|`. The URLs can come from different Uptime Kuma instances. The first URL is the default page.
- Each page ID must be unique across all instances. If the same page ID appears under two different base URLs, configuration generation fails.
- When `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS` is set, Kuma Mieru ignores `UPTIME_KUMA_BASE_URL` and `PAGE_ID`.

For examples of how Kuma Mieru parses a URL, see [Connect Uptime Kuma](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/uptime-kuma/).

### UPTIME_KUMA_BASE_URL and PAGE_ID [#uptime_kuma_base_url-and-page_id]

This is the legacy form. Kuma Mieru uses it only when `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS` is not set. All status pages come from one Uptime Kuma instance:

```ini title=".env"
UPTIME_KUMA_BASE_URL=https://example.kuma-mieru.invalid
PAGE_ID=default,status-asia
```

Separate multiple IDs in `PAGE_ID` with commas. The first ID is the default page.

## Page appearance [#page-appearance]

### Title and description [#title-and-description]

`KUMA_MIERU_TITLE` and `KUMA_MIERU_DESCRIPTION` set the title of the browser tab and the description metadata of the page (`<meta name="description">`). The `generate` script selects the values in this order:

1. The value of the environment variable. It applies to all status pages.
2. The title and description of the Uptime Kuma status page.
3. The defaults: the title `Kuma Mieru` and the description `A beautiful and modern uptime monitoring dashboard`.

If the request to the status page fails, each item that is not set uses its default.

The navigation bar title and the multi-page tabs show the live title and description of the Uptime Kuma status page first. They use the values above only when the live value is empty or the request fails.

An empty value for one of these two variables counts as set. Then the generated configuration does not use the title or description of the status page. The browser tab shows the title `Kuma Mieru`, the description is the default description, and the navigation bar still shows the live title from Uptime Kuma.

### Icon [#icon]

All icons on the page come from Uptime Kuma through the `/api/icon` proxy of Kuma Mieru. The `generate` script selects the icon address in this order:

1. The value of `KUMA_MIERU_ICON`. An empty value skips this item.
2. The icon of the Uptime Kuma status page.
3. The default icon `/icon.svg`.

`KUMA_MIERU_ICON` must point to an image on the Uptime Kuma instance of the status page:

| Value                                                                           | Result                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| A full URL with the same origin as the Uptime Kuma base URL                     | Kuma Mieru uses this image                        |
| A relative path, for example `/logo.png`                                        | Kuma Mieru appends it to the Uptime Kuma base URL |
| A URL on another domain, an address that starts with `//`, or a `data:` address | Ignored. The default icon appears                 |
| `/icon.svg`                                                                     | The default Kuma Mieru icon appears               |

The default icon also appears if the response type is not `image/*` or the image is larger than 2 MB.

<Callout type="info" title="Title, description and icon in the template">
  The `apps/web/.env.example` template contains the lines `KUMA_MIERU_TITLE`,
  `KUMA_MIERU_DESCRIPTION` and `KUMA_MIERU_ICON`. They replace the title, description and icon of
  the status page. To keep the values of the status page, delete these three lines. For the values
  in Docker, see [Docker](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/deploy/docker/).
</Callout>

### Buttons [#buttons]

| Variable                      | Default | Effect                          |
| ----------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------- |
| `KUMA_MIERU_EDIT_THIS_PAGE`   | `false` | Shows the Edit This Page button |
| `KUMA_MIERU_SHOW_STAR_BUTTON` | `true`  | Shows the Star on GitHub button |

The value `true` (in any letter case) turns a button on. All other values, including an empty value, turn it off.

With the `docker-compose.yml` of the repository, a missing `KUMA_MIERU_SHOW_STAR_BUTTON` in `.env` goes to the container as an empty value. The Star button is then hidden. To show it, write `KUMA_MIERU_SHOW_STAR_BUTTON=true` in `.env`.

### Legacy variable names [#legacy-variable-names]

If a `KUMA_MIERU_*` variable is not set, Kuma Mieru reads the matching `FEATURE_*` variable. If both are set, Kuma Mieru uses `KUMA_MIERU_*`.

| Variable                      | Legacy name                |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `KUMA_MIERU_TITLE`            | `FEATURE_TITLE`            |
| `KUMA_MIERU_DESCRIPTION`      | `FEATURE_DESCRIPTION`      |
| `KUMA_MIERU_ICON`             | `FEATURE_ICON`             |
| `KUMA_MIERU_EDIT_THIS_PAGE`   | `FEATURE_EDIT_THIS_PAGE`   |
| `KUMA_MIERU_SHOW_STAR_BUTTON` | `FEATURE_SHOW_STAR_BUTTON` |

## Upstream requests [#upstream-requests]

### ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS [#allow_insecure_tls]

Controls whether the Kuma Mieru server validates the HTTPS certificate when it requests Uptime Kuma at runtime (monitoring data, status page data and icons). The default is `false`, which validates the certificate strictly. The value `true` skips certificate validation and is a security risk. Use it only in a trusted environment with a self-signed certificate. The value must be `true` or `false` (in any letter case). Any other value makes the server fail when it loads.

This variable does not affect the requests of the `generate` script that read the title, description and icon of the status page. These requests always validate the certificate. With a self-signed certificate, this step fails, and the title, description and icon come from the environment variables or the defaults.

### Timeout and retries [#timeout-and-retries]

These variables apply to the requests that the Kuma Mieru server sends to Uptime Kuma at runtime. They do not affect the requests of the `generate` script that read the status page metadata. The icon proxy uses a fixed timeout of 10 seconds and does not read `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`.

| Variable                 | Default | Range         | Meaning                                        |
| ------------------------ | ------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`     | `8000`  | 1000 to 60000 | Request timeout, in milliseconds               |
| `REQUEST_RETRY_MAX`      | `3`     | 0 to 10       | Maximum number of retries                      |
| `REQUEST_RETRY_DELAY_MS` | `500`   | 100 to 10000  | Base interval between retries, in milliseconds |

Each value must be an integer in its range. Otherwise the server fails when it loads.

## Error handling [#error-handling]

### SSR_STRICT_MODE [#ssr_strict_mode]

Kuma Mieru only validates the value of this variable. The value must be `true` or `false` (in any letter case), and the default is `false`. Any other value makes the server fail when it loads. The variable does not change the page behavior.

### NEXT_PUBLIC_ERROR_PAGE_DEV_MODE [#next_public_error_page_dev_mode]

Controls whether the global error page shows the full stack trace. The default is `false`. The global error page appears when the root layout fails. When this variable is `true`, the global error page shows the stack trace. With `NODE_ENV=development`, the global error page always shows the stack trace. The regular error page does not read this variable. It shows the stack trace whenever the error has one.

The client can read this variable. Its value is written into the client code during `next build`, so a change needs a new build. The build stage of the Docker image does not set this variable, so you cannot turn it on with a container environment variable.

## Security [#security]

### ALLOW_EMBEDDING [#allow_embedding]

Controls whether other sites can embed the dashboard in an iframe. Kuma Mieru reads this variable at runtime, so a change needs no image rebuild.

| Value                             | Effect                                                            |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `false` or not set                | Blocks embedding. This is the default and the most secure setting |
| `true`                            | Allows any site to embed the dashboard. Not recommended           |
| A comma-separated list of origins | Allows only the same origin and the listed origins                |

```ini
# Allow the same origin and example.com
ALLOW_EMBEDDING=example.com
# Allow the same origin and multiple origins
ALLOW_EMBEDDING=example.com,app.example.com
# An origin can include the protocol
ALLOW_EMBEDDING=https://example.com
```

<Callout type="warn">
  With `true`, any site can embed your dashboard. This can allow clickjacking attacks. When
  possible, list the allowed origins.
</Callout>

### STRICT_IMAGE_REMOTE_PATTERNS [#strict_image_remote_patterns]

Controls which remote image domains `next/image` can load. It applies during `next build`.

| Value   | Effect                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `false` | Default. Allows all remote image domains                                                                                                                 |
| `true`  | Allows only the domains that the `generate-image-domains` script generates: the domains of the Uptime Kuma base URLs and the domain of `KUMA_MIERU_ICON` |

<Callout type="warn">
  The default relaxes the remote image domain restrictions. This prevents image failures when the
  Docker runtime endpoints change. In high-security environments, set
  `STRICT_IMAGE_REMOTE_PATTERNS=true` when you build your own image. The build step must be able to
  generate the complete domain allowlist.
</Callout>


# Connect Uptime Kuma (https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/uptime-kuma/)

<Callout type="info" title="Version requirement">
  Kuma Mieru is tested and compatible with the latest stable version of Uptime Kuma (v1.23.0 and
  later). If your version is older, upgrade to v1.23.0 or later as described in the [Uptime Kuma
  update guide](https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/wiki/%F0%9F%86%99-How-to-Update). Back up
  your data before you upgrade.
</Callout>

## Preparation [#preparation]

<Steps>
<Step>

### Install Uptime Kuma [#install-uptime-kuma]

Install and configure Uptime Kuma.

</Step>
<Step>

### Set the display time zone [#set-the-display-time-zone]

In the Uptime Kuma settings, set `Display Timezone` to a UTC+0 time zone.

The times that the Uptime Kuma backend sends to the frontend carry no time zone information. Kuma Mieru shows all times in UTC+0. If the display time zone is not UTC+0, the times in Kuma Mieru are offset.

</Step>
<Step>

### Create a status page [#create-a-status-page]

Create a status page in Uptime Kuma and copy its URL, for example `https://example.kuma-mieru.invalid/status/test1`.

</Step>
<Step>

### Configure the environment variables [#configure-the-environment-variables]

Put the status page URL in `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS`:

```ini title=".env"
UPTIME_KUMA_URLS=https://example.kuma-mieru.invalid/status/test1
```

Where you set it depends on the deployment method. See [Environment Variables](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/environment/).

</Step>
</Steps>

## Status page URL [#status-page-url]

Kuma Mieru splits the URL into two parts. The part before `/status/` is the base URL of Uptime Kuma. The segment after `/status/` is the page ID. If Uptime Kuma runs under a subpath, the base URL keeps the path prefix.

| Status page URL                                          | Base URL                                  | Page ID   |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------- |
| `https://example.kuma-mieru.invalid/status/test1`        | `https://example.kuma-mieru.invalid`      | `test1`   |
| `https://example.kuma-mieru.invalid/kuma/status/default` | `https://example.kuma-mieru.invalid/kuma` | `default` |

If a URL has no `/status/<page ID>` part, configuration generation fails.

## Multiple status pages [#multiple-status-pages]

Separate multiple URLs with `|`. The status pages can come from different Uptime Kuma instances:

```ini title=".env"
UPTIME_KUMA_URLS=https://example.kuma-mieru.invalid/status/default|https://status.kuma-mieru.invalid/status/secondary
```

- The first URL is the default page.
- Each page ID must be unique across all instances. If two instances both have a status page with the page ID `default`, configuration generation fails with an error that starts with `Duplicate page id "default"`. Give the status page in one of the instances a different page ID.

## How Kuma Mieru reads the data [#how-kuma-mieru-reads-the-data]

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant G as generate script
  participant K as Uptime Kuma
  participant S as Kuma Mieru server
  participant B as Browser
  G->>K: Request each status page
  K-->>G: Title, description and icon of the status page
  G->>G: Write generated-config.json
  B->>S: Open the dashboard
  S->>K: Request monitoring data
  K-->>S: Monitoring data
  S-->>B: Page
```

- The `generate` script runs during the build or when the container starts. For the details, see [Choose a Deployment Method](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/deploy/). If the script cannot reach Uptime Kuma, the title, description and icon come from the environment variables or the defaults.
- The Kuma Mieru server requests the monitoring data from Uptime Kuma at runtime. Thus the environment that runs Kuma Mieru must be able to reach the status page URL.
- If Uptime Kuma uses a self-signed certificate, see [ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/environment/#allow_insecure_tls). This variable applies to the runtime requests of the server. It does not apply to the requests of the `generate` script that read the status page metadata. With a self-signed certificate, that step fails, and the title, description and icon come from the environment variables or the defaults.
- You also set the timeout and the retry count of the runtime server requests in [Environment Variables](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/environment/).


# Cloudflare Workers (https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/deploy/cloudflare/)

<Callout type="warn" title="Not supported yet">
  Cloudflare Workers deployment is not supported yet. Use [Vercel](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/deploy/vercel/) or
  [Netlify](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/deploy/netlify/) instead. For the discussion, see
  [#88](https://github.com/Alice39s/kuma-mieru/issues/88#issuecomment-2919619066).
</Callout>

## Cloudflare configuration in the repository [#cloudflare-configuration-in-the-repository]

The web application keeps a Cloudflare build configuration based on OpenNext (`@opennextjs/cloudflare`). The files are in the `apps/web` directory:

| File                  | Content                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `wrangler.jsonc`      | Worker name `uptime-kuma-pages`, the `nodejs_compat` flag, the entry `.open-next/worker.js` and the asset directory `.open-next/assets` (binding `ASSETS`) |
| `open-next.config.ts` | The OpenNext configuration for Cloudflare                                                                                                                  |

## Scripts [#scripts]

Run these commands in the `apps/web` directory:

| Command                     | Action                                                                                                |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bun run build:cloudflare`  | Sets `CF_DEPLOYMENT=true`, runs the `generate` script, then builds with `opennextjs-cloudflare build` |
| `bun run deploy:cloudflare` | Sets `CF_DEPLOYMENT=true` and deploys with `opennextjs-cloudflare deploy`                             |

If you try it yourself, import the repository on Cloudflare and set the root directory to `apps/web`. Then set the variables as described in [Environment Variables](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/environment/).


# Docker (https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/deploy/docker/)

<Callout type="info">Docker deployment is in Beta.</Callout>

The image is `ghcr.io/alice39s/kuma-mieru:1`. It supports `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. The service in the container listens on port 3000. The examples below map it to port 3883 on the host. For the meaning of the tags, see [Versioning](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/guides/versioning/).

## Start [#start]

<Tabs items={['Docker Compose', 'docker run']}>
<Tab value="Docker Compose">

Docker Compose is the recommended method.

<Steps>
<Step>

Clone the repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Alice39s/kuma-mieru.git
cd kuma-mieru
```

</Step>
<Step>

`docker-compose.yml` reads the `.env` file in the repository root. Copy the template of the web application:

```bash
cp apps/web/.env.example .env
```

</Step>
<Step>

Edit `.env` and set at least `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS`. For the other variables, see [Environment Variables](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/environment/).

```ini title=".env"
UPTIME_KUMA_URLS=https://example.kuma-mieru.invalid/status/your-status-page-id
```

The template lines `KUMA_MIERU_TITLE`, `KUMA_MIERU_DESCRIPTION` and `KUMA_MIERU_ICON` replace the title, description and icon of the status page. Change the title and the description to the values that you need. To keep the icon of the status page, delete the `KUMA_MIERU_ICON` line.

</Step>
<Step>

Start the service:

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

The service is available at `http://0.0.0.0:3883`.

</Step>
<Step>

Show the logs:

```bash
docker compose logs -f
```

</Step>
</Steps>

<Callout type="warn" title="Missing variables in .env become empty values">
The `environment` section of `docker-compose.yml` lists the status page addresses and the `KUMA_MIERU_*` variables. If one of them is missing from `.env`, it goes to the container as an empty value and replaces the built-in default of the image:

- If neither `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS` nor `UPTIME_KUMA_BASE_URL` with `PAGE_ID` is set, the configuration script stops with an error and the container start stops.
- If `KUMA_MIERU_SHOW_STAR_BUTTON` is missing, the Star button is hidden. To show it, write `KUMA_MIERU_SHOW_STAR_BUTTON=true`.
- If `KUMA_MIERU_TITLE` or `KUMA_MIERU_DESCRIPTION` is missing, the browser tab title and the page description use the Kuma Mieru defaults.
- If `KUMA_MIERU_ICON` is missing, the icon of the status page is used.

</Callout>

</Tab>
<Tab value="docker run">

<Steps>
<Step>

Pull the image from GHCR:

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/alice39s/kuma-mieru:1
```

</Step>
<Step>

Start the container. Give the environment variables with `-e`, and set `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS` first:

```bash
docker run -d \
  --name kuma-mieru \
  -p 3883:3000 \
  -e UPTIME_KUMA_URLS="https://example.kuma-mieru.invalid/status/default|https://example.kuma-mieru.invalid/status/secondary" \
  -e KUMA_MIERU_TITLE="Kuma Mieru" \
  ghcr.io/alice39s/kuma-mieru:1
```

If `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS` is not set, the container connects to the built-in demo status page of the image. For the other built-in values, see [Built-in defaults of the image](#built-in-defaults-of-the-image).

</Step>
</Steps>

If you have many variables, write them into a `.env` file. Then use `--env-file .env` instead of many `-e` options. The `--env-file` option of the Docker CLI does not remove the quotes around a value. If you use `apps/web/.env.example` from the repository as the template, remove the quotes first. For example, change `KUMA_MIERU_TITLE="Kuma Mieru"` to `KUMA_MIERU_TITLE=Kuma Mieru`.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Built-in defaults of the image [#built-in-defaults-of-the-image]

The image sets defaults for these variables. When you start the container with `docker run`, each variable that you do not set with `-e` or `--env-file` uses its default:

| Variable                      | Default                                              |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS`            | Empty                                                |
| `UPTIME_KUMA_BASE_URL`        | `https://whimsical-sopapillas-78abba.netlify.app`    |
| `PAGE_ID`                     | `demo`                                               |
| `KUMA_MIERU_TITLE`            | `Uptime Kuma`                                        |
| `KUMA_MIERU_DESCRIPTION`      | `A beautiful and modern uptime monitoring dashboard` |
| `KUMA_MIERU_ICON`             | Empty                                                |
| `KUMA_MIERU_EDIT_THIS_PAGE`   | `false`                                              |
| `KUMA_MIERU_SHOW_STAR_BUTTON` | `true`                                               |
| `ALLOW_EMBEDDING`             | `false`                                              |

- If `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS` is not set, the container uses the built-in `UPTIME_KUMA_BASE_URL` and `PAGE_ID` and connects to the demo status page.
- The browser tab title and the page description use the environment variables or the built-in values of the image. They do not use the values of the status page. Set `KUMA_MIERU_TITLE` and `KUMA_MIERU_DESCRIPTION` to the values that you need. The navigation bar and the multi-page tabs still show the live title of the Uptime Kuma status page first. See [Environment Variables](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/environment/).
- The built-in `KUMA_MIERU_ICON` is empty, so the icon of the status page is used.
- With the `docker-compose.yml` of the repository, the variables in its `environment` section replace these defaults. See the Docker Compose notes above.

## Change the configuration [#change-the-configuration]

Each time the container starts, it runs the configuration scripts first and then starts the service. After you edit `.env`, recreate the container to apply the new environment variables:

```bash
docker compose up -d --force-recreate
```

If you use `docker run`, remove the old container. Then run `docker run` again with the new options:

```bash
docker stop kuma-mieru
docker rm kuma-mieru
```

## Update the image [#update-the-image]

<Tabs items={['Docker Compose', 'docker run']}>
<Tab value="Docker Compose">

Run these commands in the repository directory. `git pull` gets the latest `docker-compose.yml`:

```bash
git pull
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="docker run">

Remove the old container and pull the new image:

```bash
docker stop kuma-mieru
docker rm kuma-mieru
docker pull ghcr.io/alice39s/kuma-mieru:1
```

Then run `docker run` again with the same options as before.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Health check [#health-check]

The image has a health check endpoint at `/api/health`. The Dockerfile and `docker-compose.yml` both use `curl -f` to request `http://localhost:3000/api/health` in the container every 30 seconds, with a timeout of 3 seconds. `docker-compose.yml` marks the container as unhealthy after 3 failures in a row.

## Build the image yourself [#build-the-image-yourself]

If the pulled image has problems, build the image locally. Edit `docker-compose.yml`: comment out the `image` line and uncomment the `build` line:

```yaml title="docker-compose.yml"
services:
  kuma-mieru:
    # image: ghcr.io/alice39s/kuma-mieru:1
    build: .
```

Then build and start:

```bash
docker compose up -d --build
```

The Dockerfile has two stages:

| Stage   | Content                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Build   | Based on `node:26.12.1-alpine`. Installs `@kuma-mieru/web` and its workspace dependencies with Bun 1.4.4, then runs `bun run --cwd apps/web build`                                      |
| Runtime | Based on `node:26.12.1-alpine`. Runs as the non-root user `nextjs` with `dumb-init` as PID 1. At start, `tsx` runs the configuration scripts, then Node.js starts the standalone server |

`STRICT_IMAGE_REMOTE_PATTERNS` applies only when you build the image. See [Environment Variables](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/environment/#strict_image_remote_patterns).

2. Select the `Next.js` framework preset.

## Platform root directory [#platform-root-directory]

The repository is a monorepo, and the web application is in `apps/web`. When you import the repository on Vercel, EdgeOne Pages or Cloudflare, set the project root directory (Root Directory) to `apps/web`. On Netlify, set Package directory to `apps/web`; see [Netlify](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/deploy/netlify/). The platform configuration files `vercel.json`, `netlify.toml`, `edgeone.json` and `wrangler.jsonc` are in this directory.

## When the configuration applies [#when-the-configuration-applies]

The web application generates its configuration with the `generate` script. The script reads the environment variables, requests each status page to get its title, description and icon, and writes the result to `apps/web/config/generated-config.json`. Each deployment method runs this script at a different time. Thus the action after you change an environment variable is also different.

| Deployment method              | Configuration is generated                                     | After you change a variable |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Vercel, Netlify, EdgeOne Pages | During the platform build                                      | Redeploy                    |
| Docker                         | When the container starts                                      | Recreate the container      |
| Run from source                | When you run `bun run dev`, `bun run build` or `bun run start` | Run the command again       |

Some variables apply at a different time. See [Environment Variables](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/environment/).


# Netlify (https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/deploy/netlify/)

<Steps>
<Step>

### Create the site [#create-the-site]

Use one of these methods:

- Click [Deploy to Netlify](https://app.netlify.com/start/deploy?repository=https://github.com/Alice39s/kuma-mieru) and authorize GitHub when Netlify asks. Netlify creates a repository in your account.
- [Fork](https://github.com/Alice39s/kuma-mieru/fork) this repository, then import it at [app.netlify.com/start](https://app.netlify.com/start).

</Step>
<Step>

### Set the package directory [#set-the-package-directory]

In the build settings, set `Package directory` to `apps/web` and leave `Base directory` empty. Netlify installs the dependencies in the repository root, where `bun.lock` and `.nvmrc` are, and reads the build configuration file `netlify.toml` from `apps/web`. If Netlify lists more than one site in the repository when you import it, select `apps/web`.

</Step>
<Step>

### Add environment variables [#add-environment-variables]

Add `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS` with the full URL of the status page. Separate multiple URLs with `|`. For the other variables, see [Environment Variables](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/environment/).

</Step>
<Step>

### Deploy [#deploy]

Click `Deploy` to start the deployment.

</Step>
</Steps>

## Build settings [#build-settings]

`apps/web/netlify.toml` sets the build command `bun run --cwd apps/web build` and the publish directory `apps/web/.next`. Both paths are relative to the repository root. Netlify enables its Next.js adapter automatically. Apart from the package directory, the build settings need no manual changes.

## Change environment variables [#change-environment-variables]

`UPTIME_KUMA_URLS` and the related settings are written into the build output. After you change an environment variable, open `Deploys` and click `Trigger deploy` to apply the new configuration.

## Known issues [#known-issues]

<Callout type="warn" title="Build error: Could not patch functions config manifest file">
  The Netlify Next.js adapter `@netlify/plugin-nextjs` 5.16.4 can fail with `Could not patch
  functions config manifest file` while it packages the Node.js Proxy (`proxy.ts`). If the build
  fails with this error, wait until the adapter publishes a fixed version. Then redeploy.
</Callout>


# Run from Source (https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/deploy/source/)

## Requirements [#requirements]

| Tool    | Version              | Declared in                                                                     |
| ------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Node.js | 26, at least 26.12.1 | `.nvmrc` pins 26.12.1. The `engines` field of `package.json` is `>=26.12.1 <27` |
| Bun     | 1.4.4                | The `packageManager` field of the root `package.json`                           |

The build and the Node.js standalone runtime need Node.js 26, version 26.12.1 or later. The project uses Bun as its package manager. Install Bun with one of these methods:

<Tabs items={['Linux / macOS', 'Windows', 'npm']}>
<Tab value="Linux / macOS">

```bash
curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Windows">

```powershell
powershell -c "irm bun.sh/install.ps1 | iex"
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="npm">

```bash
npm i -g bun@1.4.4
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Start the development server [#start-the-development-server]

<Steps>
<Step>

### Clone the repository [#clone-the-repository]

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Alice39s/kuma-mieru.git
cd kuma-mieru
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Install the dependencies [#install-the-dependencies]

Run this command in the repository root. It installs the dependencies of all workspaces:

```bash
bun install
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Configure the environment variables [#configure-the-environment-variables]

The web application reads `.env` from the `apps/web` directory. Copy the template:

```bash
cp apps/web/.env.example apps/web/.env
```

Edit `apps/web/.env` and set `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS`:

```ini title="apps/web/.env"
UPTIME_KUMA_URLS=https://example.kuma-mieru.invalid/status/your-status-page-id
```

For multiple status pages, separate the URLs with `|`:

```ini title="apps/web/.env"
UPTIME_KUMA_URLS=https://status.kuma-mieru.invalid/status/prod|https://status.kuma-mieru.invalid/status/staging
```

The template lines `KUMA_MIERU_TITLE`, `KUMA_MIERU_DESCRIPTION` and `KUMA_MIERU_ICON` replace the title, description and icon of the status page. To keep the values of the status page, delete these three lines.

For the required variables and the other variables, see [Environment Variables](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/environment/).

</Step>
<Step>

### Start [#start]

```bash
bun run dev
```

Turborepo starts the web application and the docs site together. Open [http://localhost:3881](http://localhost:3881) to see the dashboard. The docs site runs at [http://localhost:3882](http://localhost:3882).

To start only the web application, run:

```bash
bunx turbo run dev --filter=@kuma-mieru/web
```

</Step>
</Steps>

The `dev` script of the web application runs `generate` and `lint:fix`, then starts the Next.js development server.

## Build and run the production version [#build-and-run-the-production-version]

Run these commands in the `apps/web` directory:

```bash
cd apps/web
bun run build
bun run start
```

- `bun run build` runs `generate`, then runs `next build` to create the standalone output.
- `bun run start` runs `generate` again, copies the static files into the standalone output directory, then runs `.next/standalone/apps/web/server.js` with Bun.
- The server listens on port 3000 by default.

If you run `bun run build` in the repository root, Turborepo builds the web application and the docs site together.


# Vercel (https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/deploy/vercel/)

Vercel is the recommended deployment method. You do all steps in the browser and need no server.

<Steps>
<Step>

### Fork the repository [#fork-the-repository]

1. Open the [fork page](https://github.com/Alice39s/kuma-mieru/fork) of this repository.
2. Click `Create fork`.

<Callout type="info">
  Keep your fork public. A private fork can prevent a quick sync of upstream updates. All
  configuration is in environment variables, so your fork contains none of your configuration.
</Callout>

</Step>
<Step>

### Import the repository to Vercel [#import-the-repository-to-vercel]

Open [vercel.com/new](https://vercel.com/new), find your fork and click `Import`.

![Import the repository](</kuma-mieru/_next/static/media/vercel-import.3ti7u11pp7bhz.png>)

</Step>
<Step>

### Set the root directory [#set-the-root-directory]

On the project configuration page, set `Root Directory` to `apps/web`. The web application and its `vercel.json` are in this directory.

</Step>
<Step>

### Add environment variables [#add-environment-variables]

Expand `Environment Variables` and add `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS`. Use the full URL of the Uptime Kuma status page as the value. Separate multiple status pages with `|`.

![Add environment variables](</kuma-mieru/_next/static/media/vercel-deploy.3qjqt-qnk-c4f.png>)

<Callout type="warn">
  You must set `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS` (recommended) or the legacy pair `UPTIME_KUMA_BASE_URL` and
  `PAGE_ID`. If neither is set, or a URL has no `/status/<page ID>` part, the `generate` script
  stops with an error and the Vercel build fails. For the other variables, see
  [Environment Variables](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/environment/).
</Callout>

</Step>
<Step>

### Deploy [#deploy]

Click `Deploy`.

</Step>
</Steps>

## Change environment variables [#change-environment-variables]

Vercel runs the `generate` script during the build. The script writes the environment variables and the status page data into the generated configuration. After you change an environment variable on Vercel, redeploy the project to apply it.

## Sync upstream updates [#sync-upstream-updates]

1. Open your fork on GitHub and click `Sync fork`.
2. Click `Update branch` to get the latest code from the upstream repository.

## Vercel configuration in the repository [#vercel-configuration-in-the-repository]

`apps/web/vercel.json` sets these response headers for the home page `/`:

| Header                   | Value                                             |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `Cache-Control`          | `public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=300` |
| `X-XSS-Protection`       | `1; mode=block`                                   |
| `X-Content-Type-Options` | `nosniff`                                         |


# Design Rules (https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/development/design/)

This page renders `apps/docs/design.md` from the repository. The rules are written in Chinese. Follow them when you change the interface, the styles or the link preview images of the docs site; when a rule must change, edit that file first.

## 1. 范围与优先级 [#1-范围与优先级]

- [MUST] 本文件约束 `apps/docs/` 的全部页面与浮层，以及文档构建生成的链接预览图。
- [MUST] 本文件不约束仪表盘（`apps/web/`）、README 和 GitHub 仓库页面；仪表盘的视觉由 HeroUI 主题与其组件决定，本文件只引用它的色板和字体。
- [MUST] 冲突时按以下顺序取舍：用户要求、无障碍与可用性、读者当前的任务、本项目已有约定（仪表盘的外观）、品牌表达、装饰细节。
- [MUST] 页面写什么、有哪些页、命令与配置的取值，以文档内容和代码为准；本文件只规定它们的呈现方式。

## 2. 品牌与读者 [#2-品牌与读者]

读者一边读一边在终端或托管平台里操作，需要快速找到命令、变量名和取值；中英文混排，代码与原文保持原样。

- [SHOULD] 文档站与仪表盘是同一个产品：颜色、圆角和字体取自同一个 HeroUI 主题，读者从仪表盘跳到文档时不感到换了站点。（决策：文档站贴合主程序的设计风格。来源：2026-10-25 文档站初版设计决策。）
- [SHOULD] 中性工具感：表面、文字和边框只用灰阶 token；`primary` 蓝色只出现在链接、焦点环、当前导航、主要按钮和信息提示的图标上。
- [MUST] 心跳条是唯一的品牌装饰：入口页、未找到页和链接预览图使用 `HeartbeatStrip`，颜色取仪表盘的状态色。
- [SHOULD] 页面高度由内容决定，不放全屏宣传区、插画或背景图。（决策：这是查阅型文档，不是营销页。来源：2026-10-25 文档站初版设计决策。）
- [MUST] 文案语气直接、克制：写条件、步骤和结果，不写夸张的形容词。
- [MUST] 状态同时用文字和颜色表达，不只靠颜色。

## 3. 页面结构与构图 [#3-页面结构与构图]

### 站点外壳 [#站点外壳]

- [MUST] 所有文档页共用顶栏 `SiteHeader`：高 64px，吸顶，底部 1px 边框，背景为 70% 不透明的 background 加背景模糊；内容区最大宽度 1280px，左右内边距 640px 以下 16px、640px 起 24px。
- [MUST] 顶栏左侧是品牌标识：lucide `Activity` 图标（24px，success 色，线宽 1.75），右侧依次为粗体站名、16px 高的 1px 竖线、muted 小号的站点名“文档 / Docs”。品牌标识链接到当前语言的首页。
- [SHOULD] 顶栏右侧依次为仓库入口（lucide `GitBranch`，640px 起后接“GitHub”文字）、语言切换（`Languages`）和主题菜单（显示当前选项的 `Sun`、`Moon` 或 `Monitor`）；图标 18px，按钮带可读名称。
- [MUST] 语言切换保持当前页面，只替换路径中的语言段。
- [MUST] 主题菜单是“浅色 / 深色 / 跟随系统”三项单选，标出当前项，默认跟随系统。
- [MUST] 768px 以下，顶栏右侧的图标按钮至少 44×44px。

### 长文文档 [#长文文档]

- [SHOULD] 顶栏下为 1280px 框架：1024px 起左侧为页面树侧栏（顶部是搜索框），中间为正文，1280px 起右侧为本页目录。1024px 以下页面树改为抽屉，顶栏下方 48px 的 `DocsBar` 放目录和搜索按钮，本页目录收为可展开的条。
- [SHOULD] 正文自上而下：`text-h1` 标题、`text-body` muted 描述、页面操作行（复制 Markdown、打开方式菜单，底部 1px 分隔线和 24px 间距）、正文、最后更新时间。
- [SHOULD] 页面标题用 `text-h1`；描述、侧栏、目录用 `text-body`；h2 用 `text-section-title`，h3 用 `text-card-title`；正文段落 15px、行高 1.75；行内代码和代码块用等宽字体。（决策：长文行高高于控件的 1.6，只用于文档正文。来源：2026-10-25 文档站初版设计决策。）
- [SHOULD] `Card` 为 `--radius-card` 圆角、1px 边框、16px 内边距、无阴影，卡片间隔 16px；图标用 muted-foreground 放在标题左侧，不放图标底板。可点击的卡片悬停时边框变为 40% primary，底色变为 60% accent。
- [SHOULD] `Callout` 为 `--radius-card` 圆角、1px 边框：info 与 idea 用 primary 图标；warn 用 warning 的 10% 底色和 40% 边框；error 用 danger 的 10% 底色和 40% 边框；success 用 success 图标。标题 600 字重，正文 muted。
- [SHOULD] 代码块为 `--radius` 圆角、细边框、无阴影；Tabs 的标签栏和面板是同一张 `--radius-card` 卡片，面板内不再嵌套卡片。
- [SHOULD] 同一操作有多种包管理器写法时，用包管理器标签页展示，读者的选择在各页之间保持。
- [SHOULD] 表格撑满正文宽度，表头 600 字重、muted 底色；列宽之和超过正文时，表格在外层容器内横向滚动，字号不变。
- [SHOULD] 表头不换行；某列所有正文单元格都不超过 8 个汉字或 16 个拉丁字符时，整列 `whitespace-nowrap`。（决策：自动表格布局把剩余宽度分给最长的列，中文可在任意两字之间断行，短表头会被挤成一字一行。来源：2026-10-25 文档站初版设计决策。）
- [SHOULD] Mermaid 图居中，过宽时横向滚动；渲染完成前显示 13px muted 源码；图的配色随主题切换（浅色 `neutral`、深色 `dark`）。
- [SHOULD] 截图可点击放大查看。

### 语言入口页 [#语言入口页]

- [SHOULD] 站点根路径是语言入口：页面加载后按浏览器首选语言跳到中文或英文首页，首选语言不是中文时进入英文。
- [SHOULD] 不执行脚本时显示居中的窄栏（最大宽度 448px）：心跳条、站名 `text-h1`、两张语言卡片（`text-card-title`，卡片表面与 `Card` 相同）。

### 未找到页 [#未找到页]

- [SHOULD] 居中窄栏（最大宽度 576px）：心跳条、`text-meta` muted 的“404”、中英文并列的 `text-h1` 标题、两行 muted 说明、两个返回按钮（中文为 primary 实心按钮，英文为描边按钮）。
- [MUST] 未找到页同时使用中英文，因为托管平台对所有不存在的路径返回同一个页面。

### 链接预览图 [#链接预览图]

- [MUST] 1200×630，深色 HeroUI 色板。顶部一行：左侧粗体站名（30px）加 muted 的“文档 / Docs”（24px），右侧主机名与路径前缀（22px，muted）。中间垂直居中依次为分组行、标题、描述。底部为 112px 高的心跳条带，上边 2px divider 分隔，向左渐隐（`linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 10%, #000 60%)` 遮罩）。
- [SHOULD] 字号只用于预览图：分组行 24px、行高 1.4、muted；标题 68px、行高 1.12、700 字重、`text-wrap: balance`，最多 2 行；描述 30px、行高 1.5、muted、`text-wrap: pretty`，最多 2 行。（决策：预览图在链接卡片里约缩小到 0.4 倍，字号需要放大。来源：2026-10-25 文档站初版设计决策。）
- [MUST] 限制行数的文字同时使用 `lineClamp` 和 `textOverflow: ellipsis`，截断处显示省略号。
- [MUST] 文字框离左右边缘至少 64px，文字框之间不重叠，心跳条带不压在文字上。
- [SHOULD] 分组行显示页面所在的上级目录，用“ / ”连接；末级目录与标题相同时不显示它；没有分组或没有描述时，不输出对应的行。

## 4. 视觉规则 [#4-视觉规则]

### 字体与颜色 [#字体与颜色]

- [SHOULD] 界面文字用 `--font-sans`：Noto Sans SC（拉丁字形）后接系统中文字体（PingFang SC、Hiragino Sans GB、Microsoft YaHei、Noto Sans CJK SC）；代码、命令、变量名和文件路径用 `--font-mono`（JetBrains Mono）。与仪表盘相同。
- [SHOULD] 字号只用以下角色。例外：按钮与菜单项用 14px；Fumadocs 组件自带的字号保持不变。

| 角色                 | 用途                        |
| -------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `text-h1`            | 页面标题，每页一个          |
| `text-section-title` | 文档 h2                     |
| `text-card-title`    | 卡片标题、文档 h3、语言卡片 |
| `text-body`          | 描述、正文、表格            |
| `text-meta`          | 日期、计数、次要说明        |

- [MUST] `text-meta` 不承载主要操作和限制说明。
- [SHOULD] 数值使用 tabular-nums（全局已开启）。
- [SHOULD] 颜色只用 `packages/theme/tokens.css` 的 token，它们全部取自 HeroUI 主题的 `--heroui-*` 变量；页面不写色值字面量。语义如下：

| token              | 含义                                       |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| `primary`          | 链接、焦点环、当前导航、主要按钮、信息提示 |
| `success`          | 正常、完成；品牌图标                       |
| `warning`          | 需要注意、等待中                           |
| `destructive`      | 失败、错误、不可用                         |
| `muted-foreground` | 次要文字、图标                             |

- [MUST] 文字与背景的对比度至少 4.5:1，包括 primary 文字在 10% primary 底色上（当前导航、标签页）。为此 `primary` 取 HeroUI primary 色阶的 600 档（HeroUI 在深色主题中反转色阶，浅色为较深的蓝、深色为较浅的蓝），primary 表面上的文字取 50 档。（决策：HeroUI 的 primary 默认档在深色表面和浅色底色上低于 4.5:1。来源：2026-10-25 无障碍检查。）
- [SHOULD] 代码高亮用 `github-light-default` 与 `github-dark-default` 主题，注释在代码块表面上达到 4.5:1。
- [SHOULD] 心跳条的颜色与仪表盘的状态色一致：正常为 success（按延迟分 100%、80%、60% 三档），等待为 warning，离线为 danger，维护为 60% primary。

### 布局与表面 [#布局与表面]

- [SHOULD] 内容最大宽度 1280px，与仪表盘的 `max-w-7xl` 一致。
- [SHOULD] 区块间隔 24px；卡片间隔和卡片内边距 16px；行内元素间隔 8px。
- [SHOULD] 卡片、提示框、Tabs 和浮层用 `--radius-card`（HeroUI `radius-large`）；按钮、菜单项和代码块用 `--radius`（HeroUI `radius-small`）；边框为 1px `--border`（HeroUI divider）。普通卡片不加阴影，只有浮层使用 `--shadow-overlay`。
- [SHOULD] 卡片里不再嵌套卡片。
- [MUST] 页面不横向溢出：长文本先换行或在自身区域内滚动（代码块、表格、Mermaid），不隐藏整页溢出。
- [MUST] 全局预留滚动条空间（`scrollbar-gutter: stable`），内容不随滚动条出现而横移。
- [SHOULD] 断点只用以下四个：640px（顶栏内边距与仓库文字）、768px（触控尺寸）、1024px（文档侧栏，Fumadocs 的 `md` 断点设为 1024px）、1280px（本页目录）。

### 控件与状态 [#控件与状态]

- [SHOULD] 图标按钮 `iconButton`：36px 方形，muted 图标，悬停和菜单展开时为 accent 底色；768px 以下至少 44px。
- [SHOULD] 每个操作区最多一个 primary 实心按钮；其余操作用描边或 ghost 按钮。
- [SHOULD] 复制操作在按钮上给出完成状态（图标短暂变为对勾）。
- [MUST] 每个可聚焦元素有可见的焦点样式：全局 2px `--ring` outline，偏移 2px；第三方控件去掉 outline 时补上同样的 outline。

### 动效 [#动效]

- [SHOULD] 只用 Fumadocs 自带的浮层进出动画和颜色过渡；不加滚动触发动画、视差或逐字动画。
- [SHOULD] 切换主题时不播放过渡（`disableTransitionOnChange`）。
- [MUST] 减少动效时：动画和 CSS 过渡立即完成。
- [MUST] 动效不阻挡输入和键盘导航。

### 心跳条 [#心跳条]

- [MUST] `HeartbeatStrip` 是一行等宽竖条：高 12px，条间隔 2px，条圆角 2px，条宽随容器均分；预览图中高 48px、间隔 6px、圆角 4px。
- [MUST] 心跳条是装饰：固定序列，不表示真实数据，对辅助技术隐藏（`aria-hidden`）。
- [SHOULD] 序列以正常为主，夹少量等待、离线和维护，最新的一端在右侧。

## 5. 可用原语 [#5-可用原语]

| 原语             | 位置                                        | 用途与变体                                                                                                |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SiteHeader`     | `components/site-header.tsx`                | 顶栏；`locale`                                                                                            |
| `ThemeMenu`      | `components/theme-menu.tsx`                 | 主题单选菜单（Base UI `Menu`）；`locale`                                                                  |
| `DocsBar`        | `components/docs-bar.tsx`                   | 1024px 以下的目录与搜索条，作为 `DocsLayout` 的 `header` 槽                                               |
| `iconButton`     | `components/icon-button.ts`                 | 图标按钮的类名                                                                                            |
| `Card`、`Cards`  | `components/card.tsx`、`components/mdx.tsx` | 卡片；`title`、`description`、`icon`、`href`、`external`                                                  |
| `Callout`        | `components/callout.tsx`                    | 提示框；`type`：`info`、`idea`、`warn`/`warning`、`error`、`success`；`title`                             |
| `Mermaid`        | `components/mermaid.tsx`                    | 图表；`chart`；由 Mermaid 代码块生成                                                                      |
| `HeartbeatStrip` | `components/heartbeat-strip.tsx`            | 品牌装饰；`count`（从最新一端起的条数）                                                                   |
| `OgImage`        | `lib/og-image.tsx`                          | 链接预览图模板                                                                                            |
| Fumadocs 组件    | `components/mdx.tsx`                        | `Steps`/`Step`、`Tabs`/`Tab`、`Files`/`Folder`/`File`、`Accordions`/`Accordion`、`TypeTable`、`ImageZoom` |
| 图标             | `lib/icons.tsx`                             | 侧栏与卡片可用的 lucide 图标；新图标先加入这张表                                                          |

## 6. 文案与数字格式 [#6-文案与数字格式]

- [MUST] 界面文案按页面语言显示；命令、变量名、文件路径、日志和第三方产品名保持原文，不翻译。
- [SHOULD] 标题用名词短语；按钮用动词开头的短语；描述用一句话写这一页解决的问题，不重复标题。
- [SHOULD] 第三方平台、协议和 API 名称使用官方写法（Uptime Kuma、Vercel、Cloudflare Workers、EdgeOne Pages、GitHub Pages）。
- [MUST] 示例中的密钥、令牌和私有地址使用占位值，不写真实值。
- [SHOULD] 日期显示为年、月、日；最后更新时间按页面语言格式化。

## 7. 反模式 [#7-反模式]

- [SHOULD] 不使用居中宣传标题加卡片网格的首页结构。
- [SHOULD] 不在卡片里嵌套卡片。
- [SHOULD] 不放装饰性图标底板或彩色图标背景。
- [SHOULD] 不使用原语之外的字号、字重或色值字面量。
- [SHOULD] 主要信息不用小号、低对比度的文字。
- [SHOULD] 不使用渐变；预览图心跳条带的渐隐遮罩除外。
- [MUST] 不用心跳条表示真实的服务状态。

## 8. 实现与接入 [#8-实现与接入]

- [MUST] HeroUI 主题只在 `packages/theme/hero.ts` 定义；仪表盘由 `apps/web/tailwind.config.js` 加载它，文档站由 `apps/docs/app/globals.css` 的 `@plugin '@kuma-mieru/theme/hero'` 加载它。
- [MUST] 颜色 token 与字号角色只在 `packages/theme/tokens.css` 定义；文档站在 `@import 'tailwindcss'` 之后导入它，再由 Fumadocs 的 `shadcn.css` 把颜色映射为 `fd-*`。修改主题或 token 时同时检查两个应用和预览图。
- [SHOULD] 预览图不读 CSS 变量，颜色取 `packages/theme/palette.ts` 导出的 HeroUI 深色色板；字体由 `lib/og.server.ts` 注册 `@fontsource-variable/noto-sans-sc` 的全部子集（Takumi 不读系统字体）。
- [SHOULD] 字体用 `next/font/local` 加载 Fontsource 的拉丁变量字体文件（`@fontsource-variable/noto-sans-sc`、`@fontsource-variable/jetbrains-mono`），构建不访问字体服务；变量名 `--font-noto-sans` 与 `--font-jetbrains-mono`，由 `globals.css` 的 `@theme` 组成 `--font-sans` 与 `--font-mono`。
- [MUST] 主题由 next-themes 在 `html` 上切换 `dark` 类，默认跟随系统；原生控件和滚动条使用当前主题的 color-scheme。
- [SHOULD] 文档站的 MDX 组件映射在 `components/mdx.tsx`；表头与短列由 `lib/remark-label-columns.ts` 标记为不换行；内容链接由 `lib/remark-content-links.ts` 改写为页面地址。
- [SHOULD] 浮层与菜单用 Base UI（Fumadocs 默认的组件库）；图标用 lucide-react。不引入另一套组件系统。

## 词汇表 [#词汇表]

| 概念                               | 名称                    |
| ---------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| 所有文档页共用的顶部条             | 顶栏 `SiteHeader`       |
| 顶栏左侧的图标与站名               | 品牌标识                |
| 侧栏、正文、本页目录组成的页面类型 | 长文文档                |
| 1024px 以下顶栏下方的目录与搜索条  | `DocsBar`               |
| 站点根路径的语言选择页             | 语言入口页              |
| 文档构建生成的 Open Graph 图片     | 链接预览图 `OgImage`    |
| 一行状态色竖条组成的装饰           | 心跳条 `HeartbeatStrip` |

## 待定事项 [#待定事项]

- [UNCONFIRMED] 仪表盘深色主题的 background 为纯黑；文档站长文在纯黑背景上的阅读舒适度是否需要单独的 content 色阶，尚未确认。（来源：2026-10-25 文档站初版设计决策。）


# Contributing (https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/development/)

## Requirements [#requirements]

| Tool    | Version              | Declared in                                                                     |
| ------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Node.js | 26, at least 26.12.1 | `.nvmrc` pins 26.12.1. The `engines` field of `package.json` is `>=26.12.1 <27` |
| Bun     | 1.4.4                | The `packageManager` field of the root `package.json`                           |

Turborepo reads the `packageManager` field to identify the package manager. Install Bun itself with the official install script or with `npm i -g bun@1.4.4`, not with Corepack. For the commands on each operating system, see [Run from Source](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/deploy/source/).

## Repository layout [#repository-layout]

<Files>
  <Folder name="apps" defaultOpen>
    <Folder name="web" defaultOpen>
      <Folder name="config" />
      <Folder name="messages" />
      <Folder name="scripts" />
      <File name=".env.example" />
      <File name="package.json" />
    </Folder>
    <Folder name="docs" defaultOpen>
      <Folder name="content" />
      <File name="design.md" />
      <File name="package.json" />
    </Folder>
  </Folder>
  <Folder name="packages" defaultOpen>
    <Folder name="theme" />
    <Folder name="tsconfig" />
  </Folder>
  <File name=".nvmrc" />
  <File name=".oxfmtrc.json" />
  <File name=".oxlintrc.json" />
  <File name="package.json" />
  <File name="turbo.json" />
</Files>

| Path                  | Content                                                                                            |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `apps/web`            | The Kuma Mieru web application, package `@kuma-mieru/web`                                          |
| `apps/web/config`     | The configuration schemas and the files that the `generate` script creates                         |
| `apps/web/messages`   | Interface translations, one JSON file for each language                                            |
| `apps/web/scripts`    | The `generate` script and other scripts                                                            |
| `apps/docs`           | The docs site, package `@kuma-mieru/docs`, built as a static site with Fumadocs                    |
| `apps/docs/design.md` | The design rules of the docs site. See [Design Rules](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/development/design/)                                |
| `packages/theme`      | The theme that the web application and the docs site share, package `@kuma-mieru/theme`            |
| `packages/tsconfig`   | The shared TypeScript configurations `base.json` and `nextjs.json`, package `@kuma-mieru/tsconfig` |
| `turbo.json`          | The Turborepo task definitions                                                                     |
| `.oxlintrc.json`      | The Oxlint rules                                                                                   |
| `.oxfmtrc.json`       | The Oxfmt formatting configuration                                                                 |

## Common commands [#common-commands]

Run these commands in the repository root:

| Command                | Action                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bun install`          | Installs the dependencies of all workspaces                                                                     |
| `bun run dev`          | Starts the web application (port 3881) and the docs site (port 3882) together with Turborepo                    |
| `bun run build`        | Builds all packages                                                                                             |
| `bun run lint`         | Runs the Oxlint type-aware check. One run does the lint and the type check (based on TypeScript 7 and tsgolint) |
| `bun run lint:fix`     | Fixes problems with Oxlint, then formats with Oxfmt                                                             |
| `bun run format`       | Formats the code with Oxfmt                                                                                     |
| `bun run format:check` | Checks the format and changes no files                                                                          |
| `bun run test`         | Runs the tests                                                                                                  |

To run a task for one package only, use the Turborepo `--filter` option:

```bash
bunx turbo run dev --filter=@kuma-mieru/web
```

The `dev` script of the web application runs `generate` first. Thus you must create `apps/web/.env` before you start development. For the procedure, see [Run from Source](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/deploy/source/).

### Web application scripts [#web-application-scripts]

Run these commands in the `apps/web` directory:

| Command                    | Action                                                                       |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bun run generate`         | Runs `generate:config`, `generate:domains` and `generate:banner` in sequence |
| `bun run generate:config`  | Creates `config/generated-config.json`                                       |
| `bun run generate:domains` | Creates `config/generated/image-domains.json`                                |
| `bun run generate:banner`  | Prints the startup banner and the current configuration in the terminal      |
| `bun run build:analyze`    | Builds the application and creates a bundle analysis report                  |
| `bun run start`            | Runs the built standalone server                                             |

## Code style [#code-style]

- Use Valibot for data validation.
- Write all code in TypeScript. Keep the code short and easy to read.
- Use functional and declarative patterns. Obey the DRY principle. Use early returns to reduce nesting.
- Organize a component file in this order: exports, subcomponents, helpers, types.
- Give boolean names an auxiliary verb, for example `isLoading` and `hasError`.
- Start event handler names with `handle`, for example `handleClick` and `handleSubmit`.
- Use lowercase letters and dashes for directory names, for example `components/auth-wizard`.
- Prefer named exports for components.
- Prefer interfaces. Use const maps instead of enums. Use the `satisfies` operator to validate types.
- Use React Server Components where possible and keep `'use client'` directives to a minimum. Add error boundaries to components. Use Suspense for asynchronous operations.

## Internationalization [#internationalization]

Interface translations are in `apps/web/messages/`, one JSON file for each language, for example `apps/web/messages/en-US.json`. To add a language:

1. Add the language to the `locales` array in `apps/web/utils/i18n/config.ts`.
2. Add the translation file of the language to `apps/web/messages/`.
3. Register the import of the translation file in `messageLoaders` in `apps/web/utils/i18n/messages.ts`. Kuma Mieru cannot load the translations of a language that is not registered.
4. To show a flag in the language menu, add the matching flag component from `@sankyu/react-circle-flags` to the `flagComponents` maps in `apps/web/components/basic/i18n-switch.tsx` and `apps/web/app/global-error.tsx`. Use the `alpha2Code` of the language as the key.

## Submit a pull request [#submit-a-pull-request]

<Steps>
<Step>

### Prepare the repository [#prepare-the-repository]

Fork this repository on GitHub. Then clone your fork, add the upstream repository and install the dependencies:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/kuma-mieru.git
cd kuma-mieru
git remote add upstream https://github.com/Alice39s/kuma-mieru.git
bun install
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Create a branch [#create-a-branch]

Use the `feature/` prefix for a new feature and the `fix/` prefix for a bug fix:

```bash
git checkout -b feature/amazing-feature
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Change and check the code [#change-and-check-the-code]

Test your changes with `bun run dev`. Before you commit, run:

```bash
bun run lint
bun run format
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Commit the changes [#commit-the-changes]

Write the commit message in the Conventional Commits format:

```bash
git commit -m 'feat(component): add some amazing feature'
```

| Type       | Use                                                                    |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `feat`     | A new feature                                                          |
| `fix`      | A bug fix                                                              |
| `docs`     | Documentation changes                                                  |
| `style`    | Changes that do not affect the meaning of the code, such as formatting |
| `refactor` | Code changes that neither fix a bug nor add a feature                  |
| `perf`     | Performance improvements                                               |
| `test`     | New or corrected tests                                                 |
| `chore`    | Changes to the build process or auxiliary tools                        |

</Step>
<Step>

### Push and open a pull request [#push-and-open-a-pull-request]

```bash
git push origin feature/amazing-feature
```

Then open a pull request from your fork to the main repository.

</Step>
</Steps>

A pull request must meet these requirements:

- Each pull request addresses one issue or one feature.
- The description states clearly what the pull request does.
- Interface changes include screenshots when possible.
- The code passes all lint and format checks.
- The changes work in both the light and the dark theme.
- The pull request stays current with the main branch through rebase.

## Tests and documentation [#tests-and-documentation]

- Write tests for your code when applicable and run them with `bun run test`. Your changes must not break existing features.
- If your changes affect the features, update `README.md`, `README.en.md` and the matching pages in `apps/docs/content/docs`. Update both the Chinese file (`page.mdx`) and the English file (`page.en.mdx`).
- Add comments that describe the purpose of your components.


# FAQ (https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/guides/faq/)

<Accordions type="single">
<Accordion title="Why do the times in Kuma Mieru differ from the times in Uptime Kuma?">

The times that the Uptime Kuma backend sends to the frontend carry no time zone information. To make development easier, Kuma Mieru shows all times in UTC+0.

In the Uptime Kuma settings, set `Display Timezone` to a UTC+0 time zone.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Does Kuma Mieru support Uptime Robot, Better Stack or other monitoring data sources?">

Kuma Mieru was designed to fix the shortcomings of Uptime Kuma. Thus v1 does not plan to support other monitoring data sources. v2 may add support for the APIs of other monitoring tools, such as Uptime Robot and Better Stack.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="The build fails, or the Docker container stops right after it starts">

The `generate` script stops with an error in these cases. The platform build then fails. In Docker, the start command of the container stops. With the `docker-compose.yml` of the repository, the container restarts again and again because of `restart: unless-stopped`.

- Neither `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS` nor `UPTIME_KUMA_BASE_URL` with `PAGE_ID` is set. The log shows `UPTIME_KUMA_BASE_URL is required (or set UPTIME_KUMA_URLS)` or `PAGE_ID is required (or set UPTIME_KUMA_URLS)`.
- A URL in `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS` does not contain `/status/<page ID>`. The error in the log starts with `Expected status page URL like`.
- Two status pages from different instances use the same page ID. See the next item.

If you start the container with `docker run` and do not set `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS`, the container connects to the built-in demo status page of the image. See [Docker](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/deploy/docker/). For the format of the status page addresses, see [Connect Uptime Kuma](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/uptime-kuma/).

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Configuration generation fails with Duplicate page id">

Two status pages from different Uptime Kuma instances in `UPTIME_KUMA_URLS` use the same page ID. Each page ID must be unique across all instances. Give the status page in one of the instances a different page ID.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="The page does not change after I change an environment variable">

The configuration is generated during the build or when the container starts. After you change a variable on Vercel, Netlify or EdgeOne Pages, redeploy. For Docker Compose, run `docker compose up -d --force-recreate`. For more information, see [Environment Variables](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/environment/).

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Can my fork leak my configuration?">

No. All configuration is in the environment variables of the deployment platform, not in the repository. Keep your fork public. A private fork can prevent a quick sync of upstream updates.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="The Netlify build fails with Could not patch functions config manifest file">

The Netlify Next.js adapter `@netlify/plugin-nextjs` 5.16.4 can show this error while it packages the Node.js Proxy (`proxy.ts`). Wait until the adapter publishes a fixed version, then redeploy.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="What do I do if Uptime Kuma uses a self-signed certificate?">

In a trusted environment, set `ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS=true`. The server then skips the HTTPS certificate validation of Uptime Kuma at runtime. This is a security risk.

This variable does not affect the requests of the `generate` script that read the status page metadata. These requests still validate the certificate, so the title, description and icon come from the environment variables or the defaults. Set the title and the description with `KUMA_MIERU_TITLE` and `KUMA_MIERU_DESCRIPTION`, and point `KUMA_MIERU_ICON` to the icon on Uptime Kuma. For more information, see [ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/environment/#allow_insecure_tls).

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Can I embed the dashboard in an iframe on another site?">

Yes. Embedding is blocked by default. List the allowed origins in `ALLOW_EMBEDDING`, for example `ALLOW_EMBEDDING=example.com`. For more information, see [ALLOW_EMBEDDING](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/environment/#allow_embedding).

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Remote images do not load">

The default `STRICT_IMAGE_REMOTE_PATTERNS=false` allows all remote image domains. With `true`, the allowlist contains only the domains of the Uptime Kuma base URLs and of `KUMA_MIERU_ICON`. Images from other domains do not load. For more information, see [STRICT_IMAGE_REMOTE_PATTERNS](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/configuration/environment/#strict_image_remote_patterns).

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Can I deploy to Cloudflare Workers?">

Not yet. Use Vercel or Netlify instead. For the Cloudflare configuration in the repository, see [Cloudflare Workers](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/deploy/cloudflare/).

</Accordion>
</Accordions>


# Versioning (https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/guides/versioning/)

## Recommended tag [#recommended-tag]

<Callout type="warn" title="Use the major version channel">
  For the Docker image, use `ghcr.io/alice39s/kuma-mieru:1` (the major version channel). Do not pin
  a minor or patch version (for example `:1.6` or `:1.6.2`) unless you have a clear canary and
  rollback strategy.
</Callout>

## Compatibility scope [#compatibility-scope]

- Within the `v1` major version, the project keeps forward compatibility as much as possible.
- `v2` will contain major breaking changes.

## Image tags [#image-tags]

The `Docker Build and Push to GHCR` workflow gives the image these tags, based on the version in `apps/web/package.json`:

| Tag           | Example            | Points to                                     |
| ------------- | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| Major version | `1`                | The latest build of this major version        |
| Minor version | `1.6`              | The latest build of this minor version        |
| Full version  | `1.6.2`            | The build of this version                     |
| `latest`      | `latest`           | The latest build of the default branch `main` |
| Commit        | `sha-<short hash>` | The build of one commit                       |

Each tag contains the `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` architectures. The workflow runs in these cases:

| Trigger                                                                                                        | Builds the image | Pushes the tags |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | --------------- |
| A push to `main` that changes `apps/web/package.json`, `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml` or the workflow file | Yes              | Yes             |
| A manual run, or a start from `Manual Version Bump`                                                            | Yes              | Yes             |
| A pull request to `main` that changes `apps/web/package.json` or `Dockerfile`                                  | Yes              | No              |

## Release process [#release-process]

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Manual Version Bump: update, commit and push the version"] -->|starts directly| C["Create Release"]
  A -->|starts directly| D["Docker Build and Push to GHCR"]
  M["A maintainer pushes a version commit to main"] -->|push starts| C
  M -->|push starts| D
  C --> E["v tag and GitHub Release"]
  D --> F["GHCR image"]
```

1. A maintainer runs the `Manual Version Bump` workflow manually and selects `patch`, `minor` or `major`. The workflow updates the version in `apps/web/package.json`, commits `chore(release): bump version to <version>` and pushes the commit. Then it starts `Create Release` and `Docker Build and Push to GHCR` directly.
2. A maintainer can also change the version in `apps/web/package.json` and push the commit to `main`. Then the push starts the two workflows.
3. `Create Release` reads the version in `apps/web/package.json`. If the current version is different from the version of the latest release, it creates the tag `v<version>` and a GitHub Release. The release notes contain a changelog built from the commits, a list of contributors, and the update procedures for Docker and Docker Compose.
4. `Docker Build and Push to GHCR` builds the image and pushes the tags in the table above.

## Upgrade [#upgrade]

| Deployment method              | How to upgrade                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Docker                         | Pull the new image and recreate the container. See [Docker](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/deploy/docker/)                                                            |
| Vercel, Netlify, EdgeOne Pages | Sync your fork on GitHub (`Sync fork`, then `Update branch`). See [Vercel](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/deploy/vercel/)                                             |
| Run from source                | Run `git pull` to get the latest code. Then install the dependencies and build again as described in [Run from Source](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/deploy/source/) |


# Overview (https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/)

Kuma Mieru is a third-party monitoring dashboard for Uptime Kuma, built with Next.js 16, TypeScript and Recharts. It reads the data of Uptime Kuma public status pages and shows the latency and status of each monitor in interactive charts. The built-in public status page of Uptime Kuma has no latency charts and is hard to read at a glance. Kuma Mieru adds these charts and a clearer layout.

<Callout type="warn" title="Set the Uptime Kuma display time zone to UTC+0">
  Version 1.1.4 and later use new time handling logic. In the Uptime Kuma settings, set `Display
  Timezone` to a UTC+0 time zone. For the reason, see the [FAQ](https://alice39s.github.io/kuma-mieru/en/guides/faq/).
</Callout>

## Features [#features]

- The status updates in real time, and the page refreshes automatically.
- The interface uses HeroUI components and fits screens of different sizes.
- Interactive Recharts charts show the latency and status of each node.
- Three themes are available: dark, light and system.
- The dashboard shows the incident updates and status events of the Uptime Kuma status page.
- One Kuma Mieru instance can show multiple status pages. The status pages can come from different Uptime Kuma instances.

## Tech stack [#tech-stack]

| Purpose               | Technology              |
| --------------------- | ----------------------- |
| Framework             | Next.js 16, React 19    |
| Language              | TypeScript              |
| Charts                | Recharts                |
| Components and styles | HeroUI, Tailwind CSS v4 |
| Package manager       | Bun                     |
